hypothesis_tested: Both RS execution profiles (minimal and dialogic) forbid appending advice AND a new question/probe. Permitting a brief warm close or one open question (while still forbidding advice, to preserve the family's identity) should recover quality lost to this constraint.
hypothesis_correction_before_testing: The initial narrower hypothesis (minimal profile specifically is the problem) was checked and disconfirmed before building any fix: dialogic actually lost to baseline WORSE (21/21=100%) than minimal (11/13=84.6%), because both profiles share the same no-question/no-advice constraint.
method: Regenerated the 31 Restatement-family routed replies (300l's external test) with only the RS guidance text swapped to the warm-close variant (308l) -- MS candidate, seed, dialogue, requested_action_id held byte-identical. Re-ran the same blind pairwise quality instrument (305l/306l pattern) comparing the new replies against the SAME original baseline replies.
interpretation: Real, meaningful, but partial improvement. Baseline win rate dropped 19.4 points (93.5% -> 74.2%), and a genuine EQUIVALENT verdict appeared for the first time (0/31 before, 5/31 after) -- the hypothesis was directionally correct and the fix has real effect, not noise. But it does not flip the overall conclusion: baseline still wins a clear majority (74.2%). Two compounding causes visible in remaining-loss judge rationales: (1) the warm-close instruction is not followed 100% of the time by this weak 8B generator, consistent with the ~65% RS content-following rate independently verified earlier this session -- some replies still end bare, without the permitted warm close/question; (2) even when the warm close IS added, some replies anchor their restatement to OLDER conversation content rather than the seeker's LATEST turn, reading as less responsive/in-the-moment than baseline, which naturally tends to engage with the most recent message. A few remaining-win/equivalent examples also show a genuine RS strength: in at least one case, baseline's premature move into advice-giving ('Have you considered talking to your manager or HR') was judged as adding pressure, while the routed reply's restraint was preferred -- confirming restraint is not universally a weakness, just insufficient on its own without also being current and warm.
conclusion_vs_original_claim: Still does not support the original claim that PM (RS+MS) matches or beats baseline on quality. The gap narrowed substantially with a small, targeted, well-reasoned fix, which is itself informative: the quality problem is real but not fundamental to RS/MS's mechanism -- it is fixable in degree, through card-content design, but a single instruction tweak did not fully close it. Further improvement would likely require addressing the two remaining causes identified (generator instruction-following reliability, and recency-anchoring of the restated content), which is a deeper card-design and possibly a stronger-generator question, not solved by this round.
next_scientific_action: Per explicit user direction, MP rule-based Step1 rescue is the next concrete work item. Any further RS quality work (recency-anchoring fix, stronger generator retest, broader family rebalancing) requires a separate user decision -- not pursued further in this round.
